subject: wrong position of rotated axis labels

messages.author: 166e40180306ffff
messages.subject: wrong position of rotated axis labels
parts:
Hello

Because I want to produce EPS and PDF files with embedded true type
fonts that I've installed on my system, I'm using the Cairo graphics
device. Unfortunately, rotated axis labels are out of alignment when
I'm using non-standard fonts.

Try this:
library(ggplot2)
library(Cairo)
df <- data.frame(y=1:2, x=c('a', 'bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb'))
CairoPDF()
ggplot(df,aes(x=x, y=y))+geom_bar()+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(angle=45,hjust=1,family='Times'))
dev.off()
shell.exec(paste(getwd(), 'Rplots.pdf', sep = '/'))

Is this a bug of ggplot2 or of the Cairo graphics device?

Erich

bug in the Cairo device.

Hi,

What exactly is 'out of alignment' in the output? I tried with Cairo,
pdf, and quartz and the three produced fairly similar results
(considering that the font is different with each). Admittedly the
output doesn't look great because of the unusual label, but I'm not
sure what you expect to see. Should the bbbbb... label be centered
with its corresponding tick mark on the x axis? Or is it the position
of the y label that's not good?

Best,

baptiste
